peerSolutions.title: Recursive star growth in Python
peerSolutions.author: Rahul Patel
peerSolutions.content:
The helper carries the current row as a string. It prints that row, adds one star, and calls itself for the next row. This gives the same increasing triangle without a nested loop.

A small dry run for `n = 3` is:

```text
current = ""  -> print "*"
current = "*" -> print "**"
current = "**" -> print "***"
```

The base case stops when the row number becomes larger than `n`.

```python
class Solution:
    def pattern3(self, n):
        self._print_rows(1, n, "")

    def _print_rows(self, row, n, current):
        if row > n:
            return

        current += "*"
        print(current)
        self._print_rows(row + 1, n, current)
```

For `n = 1`, only one line is printed. For `n <= 0`, the first call returns immediately.

Time complexity: `O(n^2)` because the strings printed across all rows contain a quadratic number of stars.

Space complexity: `O(n^2)` in Python because each recursive call keeps its own updated string, in addition to the recursion stack.

## Solution

class Solution:
    def pattern3(self, n):
        for i in range(n):
            for j in range(i+1):
                print(j+1,end="")
            print()
